pr_title: repart/measure/ukify: add support for OpenSSL engines/providers
pr_body:
It turns out it's mostly PKCS11 that supports the URI format,
and other engines just take files. For example the tpm2-tss-openssl
engine just takes a sealed private key file path as the key input,
and the engine needs to be specified separately.

This is how ukify is already implementing support for engines, as
that needs to support sbsign/sbvarsiglist/pesign which also use the
same pattern. So just add the same --signing-engine parameter as ukify,
and then drop the new --private-key-uri which was added solely to
distinguish between the two cases, which is no longer necessary as
there's the engine parameter specified directly now to disambiguate.

Fixes: #27935
pr_comments: With this and the mkosi PR https://github.com/systemd/mkosi/pull/2373 I can sign everything with either a TPM2 key using this engine https://github.com/tpm2-software/tpm2-tss-engine or with my Yubikey using PKCS11

so lemme get this straight there are basically three cases:

1. private key from file, we already support that with --private-key=
2. private key from openssl 1 "engine". For this we'd have to specify two things: an engine name, and engine-specific private key reference string. correct?
3. private key from openssl 3 "provider". For this we'd have to specify a single url referencing the private key, and it carries enough information that the provider module can be derived from it?

if that's indeed the case, maybe do it like this:

```c
--private-key=FILE|REFERENCE|URL
--private-key-source=file|provider|engine:ENGINE
```

and `--private-key-source=file` would be the default if the switch is not specified.

That way, to use the old pkcs11 engine, you'd use:

```c
--private-key=… --private-key-source=engine:pkcs11
```

but if you'd want to use new-style pkcs11 provider, you'd use:

```c
--private-key=pkcs11://… --private-key-source=provider
```

or however that works.

does that make any sense?

I love it

and that reference string can be anything, even a simple file path

Well, allegedly. It's purely speculative, since it doesn't work for me, so it could require additional magic incantations that I am not aware of.

> does that make any sense?

The question is rather, why? No other tool uses such a scheme (including our own, in already released versions, which need to keep working as-is), so it would be a one off and unlike everything else. What advantages does such a scheme bring, in practice?

> The question is rather, why? No other tool uses such a scheme (including our own, in already released versions, which need to keep working as-is), so it would be a one off and unlike 

well, the previous interfaces were designed with an openssl1 mindset if you so will, of course you end up with different schemes then.

> everything else. What advantages does such a scheme bring, in practice?

that it's clean, and works systematically? that it doesn't elevate a concept that the openssl maintainers consider obsolete into a first class config option of ours we can't get rid of?
We don't even need to have `--private-key-source=provider` from the start if you ask me, but doing it like this makes it trivial (from an API perspective) to add support for providers in the future.
I really hate it, but whatever
lgtm, just some naming tweaks please

issue_context.title: measure: Make it possible to use a smart card for pcrsig (openssl engine)
issue_context.body:
### Component

other

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

I'm building a Linux distro and I want to keep the `pcrsig` signing keys for my UKIs secure. The best way to do that is to put my signing keys into a YubiKey or other HSM. 

I can do so for essentially every other kind of signature I'm producing, but `systemd-measure` does not give me a way to use a pkcs11 URI

### Describe the solution you'd like

Make it possible to specify a pkcs11 URI to `systemd-measure` (and to `ukify`)

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Encrypt the private key on disk with GPG (with a Smart Card), then decrypt it right before use

### The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for

main (as of 06390e2)
comments:
gpg yuck.

but yeah, we should support an openssl "engine" for this, which could then be anything people like, including smartcards.

review_comments: btw, what about --certificate=? does this also refer to a x509 cert on the engine if specified?
Depends on the engine, so best left to the respective engine documentation
Also here it was already being used via X.509 since the beginning
Yes, it is bizarre, but with my yubikey the actual signing gets stuck unless the cert is loaded before the engine is loaded, it took a while to debug so I left a comment given how weird it is

this should be a // FIXME style comment i guess.

but I think this deserves some debugging. this is really weird...
